title: Which values leave the median of sixteen values unchanged?
description: The median of sixteen sorted values is found from the two middle values. Then one value is included, two values are included and one value is removed, each time keeping the median the same.
teaching_notes: One idea: the median sits at the middle of the sorted list, so a change keeps it when the middle values stay in place. Watch for students who think the median changes whenever the count of values changes.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 5)
video_script.why: A child who has seen the median move when a value is included now chooses values that keep it in place.
video_script.substitution: the book's sixteen sorted values with the two middle values both equal to 41
video_script.anchor: a row of the sixteen sorted values with the middle pair marked
never_show: a change to the list that moves the middle values, marked as right
maths_rules: 16 values: median = average of the 8th and 9th values
include one value: 17 values, median is the 9th value; including 41 keeps it 41
include two values: 18 values, median is the average of the 9th and 10th values; one value at most 41 and one at least 41 keep the two 41s in the middle, for example 10 and 90
remove one value: 15 values, median is the 8th value; removing one 41 leaves the 8th value as 41
check: with 10 and 90 added, the sorted list is 8, 10, 10, 19, 23, 26, 34, 40, 41, 41, 48, ... so the 9th and 10th are both 41
video_script.design: One row of sixteen sorted dots all video. The middle pair is marked, and each change is shown as a dot joining or leaving while the middle pair stays at forty one.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a row of the sixteen sorted values 8, 10, 19, 23, 26, 34, 40, 41, 41, 48, 51, 55, 70, 84, 91, 92

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.low: the first eight values appear in a row
marks.high: the last eight values appear in the row
marks.ask: the words median, include, remove appear with empty boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the median.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Sixteen values are written in order. Eight, ten, nineteen, twenty three, twenty six, thirty four, forty, forty one.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Then forty one, forty eight, fifty one, fifty five, seventy, eighty four, ninety one, ninety two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the median. Then say which values can be included or removed without changing it.

beats.on_screen: the row of values and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the median is the middle of the sorted values; an even count gives two middle values, an odd count gives one

marks.mid: the middle of the row is marked
marks.even: an even count of dots shows a pair in the middle
marks.odd: an odd count of dots shows a single dot in the middle

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>As before, the median sits in the middle of the sorted values.
<bookmark mark='even'/>An even count of values gives two middle values, and the median is their average.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>An odd count gives one middle value, and that is the median.

marks.given: the sixteen values are written in a line

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, sixteen values are already in order.

beats.on_screen: To find: the median; a value to include; two values to include; a value to remove, all keeping the median

marks.find: the four things to find are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the median, and then include or remove values without changing it.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Step one, sixteen is even, so the median is the average of the eighth and ninth values. Both are forty one.
<bookmark mark='avg'/>Their average is forty one.

marks.add: a new dot at 41 joins the middle

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, include one value. Include forty one, and there are seventeen values.
<bookmark mark='ninth'/>The median is now the ninth value, and it is still forty one.

beats.on_screen: include 10 and 90: 18 values, the 9th and 10th are 41 and 41

marks.two: a dot at 10 joins the left and a dot at 90 joins the right
marks.mid: the 9th and 10th values are circled as 41 and 41

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, include two values, one on each side. Take one value at most forty one and one at least forty one, such as ten and ninety.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>There are eighteen values, and the ninth and tenth are both forty one.

marks.gone: one of the two 41s leaves the row

narration: <bookmark mark='gone'/>Step four, remove one value. Remove one of the two forty ones, and fifteen values are left.
<bookmark mark='eighth'/>The median is the eighth value, and it is still forty one.

beats.on_screen: check: with 10 and 90 added, the sorted list 8, 10, 10, 19, 23, 26, 34, 40, 41, 41, ... has 41 as its 9th and 10th values

marks.count: the sorted list is counted dot by dot up to the 10th

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Check one case by counting. Add ten and ninety, and the list starts eight, ten, ten, nineteen.
It goes on with twenty three, twenty six, thirty four, forty.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The next two values, the ninth and tenth, are both forty one. The middle has not moved.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Median = 41; include 41; include 10 and 90; remove a 41
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The median is forty one. Include forty one, or include ten and ninety, or remove a forty one.
